preconditions.description: The number of nodes n is between 1 and 10,000 inclusive.
The graph is a list of length n+1, where index 0 is unused and indices 1 to n represent nodes.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(graph[i], (list, set)) for i in range(n + 1))
preconditions.description: Each element in the graph list is a collection (list or set) representing adjacency.

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= neighbor <= n for neighbor in graph[i]) for i in range(n + 1))
preconditions.description: All neighbors referenced in the adjacency list are valid node indices between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(neighbor in graph[neighbor_idx] for i in range(1, n + 1) for neighbor in graph[i] for neighbor_idx in [neighbor])
preconditions.description: The graph is undirected: if node A lists node B as a neighbor, node B also lists node A.

preconditions.expression: len(set().union(*[set(graph[i]) for i in range(1, n + 1)])) == n - 1
preconditions.description: The graph has exactly n-1 unique edges, consistent with a tree structure.

preconditions.expression: len([i for i in range(1, n + 1) if graph[i]]) > 0 if n > 1 else True
preconditions.description: The graph is connected (implied by being a tree with n nodes and n-1 edges).

postconditions.description: The return value is an integer.

postconditions.expression: return_value == sum(1 for i in range(1, n + 1) for j in range(i + 1, n + 1) if (dist(i, j, n, graph) % 2 == 0))
postconditions.description: The return value equals the count of unique pairs (i, j) with i < j such that the distance between them in the tree is even.
